item.content:encoded:
As streamers go, Netflix has one of the very best collections of original romance movies. The streaming platform is the home of modern romance classics like Set It Up, the To All the Boys I've Loved Before trilogy, The Wrong Paris, and People We Meet on Vacation. Netflix's romance movies are known for having well-written characters that are easy to get attached to, as well as compelling dynamics and strong chemistry between these characters.
While Netflix has a number of romance movies that are pretty much universally beloved, it also has some truly excellent ones that have slipped through the cracks over the years. These movies have clever main premises, strong dialogue, and captivating romances. These are forgotten Netflix romance movies that are truly perfect from start to finish.
'Along for the Ride' (2022)
Based on the Sarah Dessen novel of the same name, Along for the Ride follows a recent high school graduate named Auden (Emma Pasarow) who goes to stay at her father's home in a beach town called Colby, North Carolina for the summer. Auden is very ambitious and academic-minded, so she's missed out on most normal teenage experiences. Auden is already starting at her dream college in the fall, so now, she has the summer off to catch up on some of the things that she has missed out on.
Very quickly, Auden gets a job, makes some friends, and starts spending her nights going on mini-adventures with fellow insomniac Eli (Belmont Cameli). Auden's father (Dermot Mulroney) is more interested in writing his latest novel than parenting either her or his newborn baby, and Auden doesn't know how to connect with his wife (Kate Bosworth), so she spends more time out and about than at home. As Eli helps her check off items on the list of things she missed, the two start to really get to know each other. Auden and Eli's nights together are a bubble away from the more difficult things in their lives, though, and they soon realize that these outside obstacles could threaten their new connection. Along for the Ride is a sweet and cozy summer romance, and it remains severely underrated four years after it was released.
'Someone Great' (2019)
Someone Great is a beautiful movie with a romance that takes place out of order. Music journalist Jenny (Gina Rodriguez) is preparing to move from New York City to San Francisco for her dream job, and her boyfriend of nine years, Nate (Lakeith Stanfield), has just broken up with her. Thus, Jenny's two best friends, Blair (Brittany Snow) and Erin (DeWanda Wise), decide to cheer Jenny up and send her off by all having one last big adventure together before she moves.
Over the course of one life-changing day, Jenny, Blair, and Erin all reevaluate their paths and love lives. For Jenny, this means looking back on her memories with Nate and trying to determine where it all went wrong. For Blair, this means attempting to finally break up with Will (Alex Moffat), her boyfriend with whom she's no longer in love. Erin, meanwhile, has found a real connection with her new girlfriend, Leah (Rebecca Naomi Jones), but she is afraid to actually commit to her. Someone Great is an excellent movie that divides its romantic storylines amongst its three leads, taking them each on a journey to determine whether they want to fight for their relationships.
'Candy Jar' (2018)
Candy Jar is a coming-of-age romantic comedy about two high school debate team rivals, Lona (Sami Gayle) and Bennet (Jacob Latimore). They are the only two members of their school's debate club, and they are competing to become the club's president in order to look good to colleges. When they are reluctantly made co-presidents, Lona and Bennet start spending more time together, and they begin to question their previous impressions of each other.
Candy Jar is a funny and sweet rivals-to-lovers movie that is perfect for romance fans. Lona and Bennet are the only people who really understand each other, but their similarities also act as an obstacle to their romance. Both of their mothers put pressure on them to be the best no matter what, and they both worry about the potential risks that compromising and setting their rivalry aside could have on their futures.
'Love at First Sight' (2023)
Based on the novel The Statistical Probability of Love at First Sight by Jennifer E. Smith, Love at First Sight follows two college students who meet at JFK airport while preparing to board a flight to London. Hadley (Haley Lu Richardson) is on her way to the second wedding of her father, whom she still resents for moving away so quickly after his divorce from her mother. Oliver (Ben Hardy) is going home for a family event, although he's vague with her about the specifics. Hadley and Oliver immediately strike a connection, and they get to know each other better on the plane.
When a technological mishap prevents Hadley from saving Oliver's number after the flight, they're separated, and she is determined to find her way back to him. Oliver, meanwhile, unknowingly waits to hear from her. Love at First Sight is a really sweet and emotional movie that questions the possibility of the concept of love at first sight through the story of Hadley and Oliver. The two barely know each other, but they both take a number of risks and bold swings in order to fight for the possibility of their romance.
'Wedding Season' (2022)
Wedding Season is a fantastic fake-dating romantic comedy that follows Asha (Pallavi Sharda), a woman who recently both ended her engagement and left her face-paced job on Wall Street to work for a New Jersey-based startup. When Asha's mother pressures her to set up an online dating profile, she meets Ravi (Suraj Sharma), but their date doesn't go well. After the two cross paths at a wedding, though, Asha asks Ravi to fake a relationship with her for the remainder of the weddings that they both have to attend that summer.
Thus, Asha and Ravi go to the rest of the weddings together that summer, pretending to be a couple so that their families no longer put pressure on them. Asha, in particular, isn't looking for love, and is much more determined to prove herself at work. Still, though, she and Ravi start to really start to form a connection through their fake relationship. The only problem is, there is a ticking clock on their fake romance, and Asha starts to realize that she might not be ready for it to end. Wedding Season is such a fun and swoonworthy rom-com, and romance fans who love wedding movies will really enjoy this one.
'The Lovebirds' (2020)
The Love Birds is an action rom-com that starts with a breakup. Leilani (Issa Rae) and Jibran (Kumail Nanjiani) once had the perfect romance. Now, though, it's been four years, and they fight all the time. Finally, on the way to a dinner party, Jibran and Leilani decide to break up. Seconds later, though, they hit a cyclist with their car. The cyclist then refuses their help, and another man steps in and kills him with their car, pulling a confused Leilani and Jibrani into a dangerous conspiracy.
Worried that they will be blamed for the man's death, Leilani and Jibran decide to pursue the conspiracy and solve his murder. The more entangled the former couple gets in this investigation, though, the more danger they find themselves in. The Lovebirds is an absolutely hilarious movie with a compelling action plot and an excellent second chance romance, where Leilani and Jibran start to see each other in a new light thanks to the life-and-death stakes at play.
'The Half of It' (2020)
The Half of It is a Cyrano de Bergerac-inspired coming-of-age movie about a teenage girl named Ellie Chu (Leah Lewis). Ellie lives in a small town called Squahamish, and since the death of her mother years earlier, she helps her father support the two of them by writing her classmates' essays for money. One day, Ellie's neighbor, Paul Munsky (Daniel Diemer), offers to pay her to write a love letter to his crush, the popular Aster Flores (Alexxis Lemire). Despite her own secret crush on Aster, Ellie agrees to it, but the letter quickly spirals into constant texting.
The Half of It has everything: a beautiful coming-of-age story, a lovely and unexpected friendship between Ellie and Paul, and a complicated love square involving the two of them, Aster, and her boyfriend. The romance between Ellie and Aster develops completely through writing, with Ellie feeling conflicted over the lie that brought them together in the first place. Meanwhile, Aster believes that Paul is the one that she is falling for.

item.title: [Bollywood Hungama] #Love: Arjun Das and Aishwarya Lekshmi starrer Netflix new-age romance to premiere on October 2
item.dc:creator: Bollywood Hungama News Network
item.description: Netflix is set to bring a contemporary take on romance with its upcoming Tamil series #Love, which will premiere on October 2. Produced by showrunner Soundarya Rajinikanth and directed by Balaji Mohan, the series stars Arjun Das and Aishwarya Lekshmi in a fresh on-screen pairing. #Love: Arjun Das and Aishwarya Lekshmi starrer Netflix new-age romance to premiere on October 2 Set against the world of dating apps, #Love revolves around Tara and Matthew, two rival founders behind the dating platform
item.content:encoded:
Netflix is set to bring a contemporary take on romance with its upcoming Tamil series #Love, which will premiere on October 2. Produced by showrunner Soundarya Rajinikanth and directed by Balaji Mohan, the series stars Arjun Das and Aishwarya Lekshmi in a fresh on-screen pairing.
#Love: Arjun Das and Aishwarya Lekshmi starrer Netflix new-age romance to premiere on October 2
Set against the world of dating apps, #Love revolves around Tara and Matthew, two rival founders behind the dating platforms FOUND and Find My Bae. While the two have built businesses around helping people find love and compatibility, their own relationship is set to put their theories to the test.
The series explores the question of whether chemistry or compatibility ultimately matters more in a relationship, while also looking at how romance and connections have evolved in the age of dating apps, swipes, matches and unread messages.
Monika Shergill, Vice President, Content, Netflix India, said, “This has been a defining year for Netflix India, as we’ve deepened our investment in storytelling from the South of India — and #Love is a title we’re especially excited about. As we expand our slate across Tamil storytelling, this contemporary, feel-good rom com stood out as a genre and that was ready for a fresh, confident take. ##Love steps into that space with a modern, chemistry-driven love story about two rival dating-app founders who end up testing their own theories of love on each other. Director Balaji Mohan, together with showrunner and producer Soundarya Rajinikanth, brings a wonderfully playful perspective to the series, while Arjun Das and Aishwarya Lekshmi bring the central relationship to life with chemistry, warmth and humour. The series captures that giddy, unguarded feeling of falling for someone you never saw coming - funny, warm, and exhilarating to anyone who's ever overthought a text message.”
View this post on Instagram
Speaking about the series, showrunner and producer Soundarya Rajinikanth said, "What drew me to #Love was how effortlessly it captures relationships today without losing its warmth and emotion. Balaji has created characters who are ambitious, flawed and incredibly easy to root for, and Arjun and Aishwarya bring such a refreshing energy to them. It's exactly the kind of contemporary story we were excited to bring to audiences with Netflix."
Director Balaji Mohan added, "When we made #Love, we wanted to tell a story that feels like it belongs to today. Romance has evolved, the way we meet people has changed, but the emotions at the heart of relationships remain incredibly familiar and timeless. What I love about this series is that it isn't only about two people falling for each other – friendship, family, ambition and finding yourself are equally important parts of their journeys."
#Love is written by Nirmal Williams, with Sharada Subramanian and Shweta Chakravarty serving as co-writers. The series is produced by May6 Entertainment Factory.
With Arjun Das and Aishwarya Lekshmi coming together for the first time in this pairing, #Love promises to explore modern romance through the lens of two people whose professional rivalry could lead to an unexpected personal connection.
#Love premieres October 2, only on Netflix.

item.content:encoded:
Listen to this article in summarized format
Streaming details of Tamil series #Love
#Love will premiere on Netflix on October 2, 2026. The series will be available in Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam, giving viewers across multiple South Indian language markets a chance to watch the new romantic drama.
At the centre of #Love is a question that has become increasingly relevant in the world of modern dating, should people look for chemistry or compatibility when choosing a partner?
The series uses the dating-app world to explore this debate. Its story follows characters who have their own ideas about what makes a relationship work. While chemistry can create an immediate connection between two people, compatibility may determine whether that relationship can survive in the long run.
Aishwarya Lekshmi plays a single dating-app CEO
Aishwarya Lekshmi plays Tara, a woman who runs a dating app but is single herself. Her professional life revolves around helping people find potential partners, but her personal life does not appear to follow the same formula.
Arjun Das plays the other central character. In the latest glimpse, his character questions Tara about her belief that compatibility is enough for a successful relationship. Tara argues that if two people are genuinely compatible, chemistry will eventually follow. Their exchange sets up the central debate of the series while also giving the romance a light and conversational tone.
The new pairing of Aishwarya Lekshmi and Arjun Das is another major attraction.
More about #Love
#Love is directed by filmmaker Balaji Mohan, known for his work in Tamil cinema. The series is showrun and produced by Soundarya Rajinikanth, daughter of superstar Rajinikanth.
The series is produced by May6 Entertainment Factory. It is written by Nirmal Williams, with Sharada Subramanian and Shweta Chakravarty serving as co-writers.
The makers announced #Love earlier this year as part of Netflix India’s slate of upcoming releases for 2026. Along with the announcement, the streaming platform released a teaser that introduced the dating-app setting and the romantic conflict at the centre of the story.
The latest announcement has now confirmed the release date and languages. For Aishwarya Lekshmi, #Love marks an important career milestone as her digital debut. The actress has worked across Malayalam and Tamil cinema.
Arjun Das, meanwhile, joins her in what looks like a different kind of romantic pairing for both actors. The series uses their characters’ differing opinions about love to build its central conflict.
#Love premieres October 2, 2026, on Netflix. The series will stream in Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam. Stay tuned!

item.content:encoded:
The Ralph Lauren womenswear brand is a love letter to the designer’s wife of more than 60 years.
Ricky Lauren, his lifelong muse, is present in each of the designer’s collections.
At the designer’s New York Fashion Week show, Ricky Lauren sat front row along with other members of the Lauren family as her husband took guests on a whirlwind romantic escape ahead of the official launch of New York Fashion Week.
Actors Meghann Fahy, Cynthia Erivo, Viola Davis, Elizabeth Debicki and Ella Hunt were a few of the celebrity guests in attendance at the downtown Manhattan show.
“Ralph just generally designs so beautifully for a woman’s body,” Hunt told The Associated Press after the show.
Lauren pared down the lavish setting from his fall ready-to-wear show of opulent rugs and antique chairs, keeping the setting white and minimalist with attendees sitting on ivory fabric benches and models emerging from behind white doors.
Models glided down the rows of fashionable guests in soft and sensual silhouettes with a color palette of navy and white to the tunes of love songs, including “Every Little Thing She Does Is Magic” by The Police.
For Lauren, the collection was an “irreverent take on romance” that “upends traditional notions of chic.”
“It’s about ways of dressing that celebrate ingenuity, character, and originality — the freedom and fun of creating a style that is truly personal,” the designer said in his show notes.
Lauren opened the show with a white corseted top and white tailored pants before an array of deep, rich blues unfurled down the runway.
The 86-year-old designer played with his signature tailored designs incorporating billowing white pinstriped pants and dramatic floor-length overcoats.
Lauren accentuated his refined looks with touches of flair from oversized flowered brooches, feathered bolero jackets draped over evening gowns with plunging necklines to fringed scarves tied at the waist. While some models strutted in heels, others walked the runway in slipper-like flats. Either way, the models looked ready to jet off on a European getaway in their elegantly laid-back white pants and straw hats or pose on a red carpet in his evening gowns.
“What Ralph Lauren is doing this year is writing through his clothes about a very kind of modern dream,” David Lauren, the label’s chief branding and innovation officer, said.
In his classic take of mixing the masculine and feminine, Lauren overlaid a golden fringed gown over a pair of navy trousers, and in an homage to his first suit for women, the designer featured two pantsuits in his collection.
Lauren even brought out a youthful side to his modern romance story, pairing slim-fitting jackets with low-slung pants and distressed denim.
“What I love about coming to a Ralph Lauren show and wearing Ralph Lauren is that no matter where I am in time or space, or as I’m growing and changing in my styles and preferences and tastes change, I can grow with Ralph,” Ariana DeBose said.
The stylish crowd was eager to catch a glimpse of Lauren as the line of models returned behind the doors to close the show. As the applause rang out, Lauren arrived in his aviator glasses and varsity jacket to wave to his guests before his wife, Ricky, joined him with a kiss.
Associated Press journalist Brooke Lefferts contributed to this report.
